blind_spots_patched: Original Chapters 1–6 omitted off-balance-sheet JV corporate guarantees (₹80 Cr for ARC), massive related-party receivable buildup with ARC (~₹196 Cr owed on ~₹160 Cr FY26 parent sales), the statutory auditor's Key Audit Matter on trade-receivable ECL provisioning, and the fact that 75% (₹130.50 Cr) of the June 2025 convertible warrants remained unreceived ahead of a December 29, 2026 deadline.

Original Chapters 2 and 3 discussed defence customers generically without quantifying single-contract HAL backlog concentration (~47% of standalone backlog in one Uttam AESA radar contract), top-3 sovereign revenue concentration (>50% from DRDO and BEL/DPSUs), or the fact that FY26's 11.9% 'Exports' line now consists predominantly of deemed exports to the domestic ARC JV.

Original Chapter 1 flagged the 6.54% promoter stake and MD transition but missed recent insider equity trimming by Whole-Time Director of Strategy Atim Kabra (-0.41 percentage points in Q2 FY27 to 3.12%) and the ₹1.36 Cr unexpired-tenure cash payout to departing MD S. Gurunatha Reddy.
assumptions_changed: CONFIRMED: Astra Rafael Comsys (ARC) 50:50 JV scaled to ~₹360 Cr FY26 revenue and ₹622–636 Cr backlog as a secondary SDR/EW growth engine.
CONFIRMED: Astra is demerging its Space, Meteorology, and Hydrology verticals into Astra Space Technologies Limited (ASTL) under outgoing MD S. Gurunatha Reddy.
WEAKENED: Management guided for ₹250–₹350 Cr FY27 Free Cash Flow and near debt-free status within 1–1.5 years after FY26's +₹387 Cr CFO release.
WEAKENED: In May 2025, Astra allotted ~20.13 lakh convertible warrants at ₹864/share to raise ₹173.99 Cr.
